status: Curated primary guidance adapted to this role; live performance and qualified evaluation pending

sources.title: Max Wertheimer, Laws of Organization in Perceptual Forms (1923), English translation, university mirror

principles.sourceSummary: Visual emphasis and spatial organization help establish a reading order.
principles.application: Give the primary message one focal point; balance mass, scale and empty space.
principles.limits: UI guidance is a practice reference, not a universal advertising grid.
principles.syntheticExample: One product silhouette balances a short headline.
principles.counterexample: Five equally large elements compete; no primary takeaway.

principles.sourceSummary: Proximity and similarity affect perceived grouping; factors can reinforce or compete.
principles.application: Group a qualifier with its claim; separate unrelated signals.
principles.limits: Original perception examples do not predict conversion or universal reading order.
principles.syntheticExample: A capacity qualifier sits visibly beside the capacity line.
principles.counterexample: A qualifier appears under an unrelated lifestyle claim.

principles.sourceSummary: Text contrast, size and rendering affect accessibility; images of text are covered by the contrast guidance.
principles.application: Review full output at actual viewing size, including mandatory small print.
principles.limits: WCAG is a web accessibility reference, not publisher certification; fonts and contrast need rendered measurement.
principles.syntheticExample: Short high-contrast headline with comfortably visible qualifier.
principles.counterexample: Tiny pale text looks acceptable only when zoomed in.

principles.sourceSummary: Typography guidelines describe type scale, line height and language-specific needs.
principles.application: Specify hierarchy, alignment, font constraints and clear text zones without rewriting copy.
principles.limits: Do not copy a UI type scale as a mandatory ad specification; actual font fidelity remains untested.
principles.syntheticExample: Brand font supports two clear line lengths.
principles.counterexample: External reference type replaces the supplied brand font.

principles.sourceSummary: The Material color system uses coordinated primary and accent roles and checks foreground/background accessibility.
principles.application: Assign palette roles consistent with supplied rules and scene contrast.
principles.limits: This does not establish universal emotional effects or a sales lift from any hue.
principles.syntheticExample: Brand accent marks the focal area; quiet background protects reading.
principles.counterexample: A mood board forces forbidden colors into the brand identity.

principles.sourceSummary: Imagery guidance relates subject, focus and visual treatment to communication.
principles.application: Describe concrete scene, crop, light, camera angle and truthful product identity.
principles.limits: Editorial application to ads is a hypothesis; identity and implied claims need semantic review.
principles.syntheticExample: Ordinary departure setting supports the essentials concept.
principles.counterexample: Medical setting implies a benefit absent from product evidence.

principles.sourceSummary: Consistent visual treatment and typography support a coherent visual language.
principles.application: Lock supplied identity assets and execution rules across both routes.
principles.limits: Consistency is a practice inference here; no measured distinctive-asset strength is known.
principles.syntheticExample: Exploration changes setting while preserving the supplied product and logo.
principles.counterexample: External bottle appearance or logo leaks into the execution.

principles.sourceSummary: Layout and typography guidance require attention to the presentation context.
principles.application: Recompose focal point, reading flow and density for each pinned placement; retain source tiers and unknowns.
principles.limits: Publisher requirements come only from the separately versioned placement package; no universal safe margin is assumed.
principles.syntheticExample: A compact placement receives a simpler scene with exact copy still legible.
principles.counterexample: A tall poster is naively shrunk into a tiny banner.
